title: Safety Weave and Interlock — Field Notes (WIP)
body:
Context / intent:
This doc captures an operational draft for weaving multiple safety controls (observability, human interlocks, automated gates) into small-batch canaries and A/B runs. Goal: reduce blast radius while preserving the ability to detect subtle behavioral drift in LLM-powered routes (rerankers, generative assistants, structured generation).

Audience:
- Release stewards, oncall SREs, product PMs, solutions eng who own rollout comms
- Not a policy doc — this is tactical runbook + design notes for playbook authors

High-level pattern (one-liner):
- Run tiny, orthogonal canaries with progressive exposure; interlock signals across latency, cost, semantic-safety, and business metrics; require explicit human confirmations when cross-signal cohesion breaks.

Quick glossary (local terms):
- Safety weave = composite of automated checks + human gates + smart fallback routing
- Micro-batch = <=1% traffic slice, controlled for region + cohort + channel
- Signal chord = set of signals we require to move from step->step (latency, p95, error-rate, semantic-score, conversion)

Operational recipe (stepwise):
1) Preflight (0%):
- Create rollout hypothesis (metric delta expectations, primary metric, guardrail metric). Link to hypothesis template (confluence:ROLL-1423).
- Determine micro-batch slices: dimension by locale, device, intent-type. Prefer orthogonal slice selection to avoid correlated noise.
- Generate synthetic probes and deterministic testcases for known failure modes (safety-critical prompts, hallucination checks).
- Decide fallback model variants and autoscale budget for canary period.

2) Micro-exposure (<=0.5% traffic):
- Route synthetic + live traffic (synthetic weight 20% of slice)
- Monitor primary signal chord:
  - latency p95 <= SLO threshold (15th percentile baseline)
  - error-rate (5xx + inference timeouts) <= baseline + 0.2% absolute
  - semantic-safety score (auto-eval batch) >= baseline - 0.5 points
  - business metric (CTR/relevancy proxy) not degraded by >1.5%
- Run automated scoring every 3m and publish to canary dashboard.
- If any single metric crosses soft-warning, trigger team notif but continue monitoring. If cross-signal failure (>=2 signals breach) move to human-interlock.

3) Human-interlock & Triage:
- Who: release steward (owner), oncall SRE, model owner, product PM.
- Human interlock checklist: reproduce locally (use test harness), check KV-cache behavior, check tokenization edge cases, verify routing policies in console.
- If triage identifies safe mitigation (traffic-shed to fallback), steward approves automated rollout to rollback path. Document decision in rollout log (jira:ROLLOUT-981).
- If unresolved, escalate to oncall principal and halt progression.

4) Gradual expansion (0.5% -> 5% -> 20%):
- Expand only after 24-48h of green signal runs and no latent degradation in weekly-lookback metrics.
- Increase slice diversity (add new cohorts) rather than increase weight of same slice to catch distributional drift.
- At each expansion require: automated smoke test, canary eval run (semantic/regression tests), and steward signoff.

5) Post-mortem & metric decay watch (after 7d):
- Run post-deploy evaluation against held prompt sets.
- Check sample entropy and distribution shifts (embedding drift) and compare model-level latency cost curves.
- If business metric degradation emerges after 48–72h, trigger rollback matrix and revert to previous variant.

Observability / signal catalog (practical):
- Telemetry streams: per-token latency, request-level tail latency, model-version, route, shard, queue-depth.
- Functional evals: auto-regression suite (precision/recall-type scores), hallucination detectors (fuzzy match to ground truth bank), toxicity and policy classifiers.
- Business proxies: short-term CTR, conversion funnel step completions, usage frequency.
- Synthetic probes: deterministic prompts that exercise corner cases. Run every 5m in canary timeframe.
- Degrade signal detector: rolling-window anomaly detector that flags multivariate anomalies (example heuristic: Z-score on embedding-distance + sudden p95 jump).

Guardrail thresholds (examples — tuning required):
- Latency p95: no more than 1.4x baseline across same slice. Soft-warning at 1.2x.
- Error-rate: absolute increase <= 0.2% (soft), >=0.5% (hard)
- Semantic drift: automated eval AUC drop <= 0.02 (soft), >=0.05 (hard)
- Business metric: relative drop >1.5% (soft), >3% (hard)

Automation primitives we should build: (todo list)
- Canary dashboard that composes the signal chord and annotates correlated noise vs systemic breaks.
- One-click traffic-shed to fallback variant + audit trail.
- Canary traffic simulator to run offline experiments reproducing live load patterns.
- Canary-run ticket template generator that pre-populates hypothesis + slices + linked PRs.

Who owns what (quick owners):
- Release steward: product PM (owns hypothesis + comms)
- Canary ops + runbooks: Release Engineering & SRE (owns automation, dashboards)
- Model rollouts & fallback variants: Applied ML / Model infra (owns variant build & quant profiles)
- Eval suites + data: Research/Applied ML (owns testbank, probes)

Common failure modes & rapid mitigations (field notes):
- Symptom: Quiet degradation in downstream business metric after 2 days.
  - Likely causes: distributional drift in user intents, caching mismatch, telemetry misattribution.
  - Quick mitigation: quarantine cohort(s) with highest delta, route to previous variant, run high-priority post-deploy eval.
- Symptom: Spikes in hallucination classifier false-negatives
  - Likely causes: tokenization changes, quantization noise, prompt-change surface area.
  - Mitigation: reduce model temperature, enable stricter policy filter, or route to higher-quality variant.
- Symptom: Oscillating latency due to batch sizing
  - Mitigation: enforce per-route batching cap and enable immediate shed when queue depth > threshold.

Unresolved questions / design decisions to discuss:
- How to balance synthetic probe weight vs real traffic in micro-slices? (current bias: use 15–25% synthetic to increase signal SNR)
- Where to put the steward signoff UI? integrated into console or separate checklist in Confluence?
- Should we require multi-day green windows for business metrics or allow faster cadence for low-risk non-core features?
- Policy for canaries that cross-region (data residency implications) — need legal input.

Runbook snippets (copy/paste friendly):
- Emergency rollback cmd: (console) POST /rollouts/{id}/route?action=shed&target=fallback --body{"percent":100,"note":"auto-shed due to signal chord breach"} (ops-only endpoint).
- Canary synthetic runner: python infra/canary/run_probe.py --slice=slice-id --suite=core-failures --repeat=500

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts (raw):
- Try orthogonal slicing in the next experiment: by intent-type + device-os rather than region. Might reveal hidden correlations we've missed.
- We should add a ‘signal weight’ config to the canary dashboard so PMs can tune which metrics gate expansion.
- Consider a temporary feature-flag that flips routing to fallback for N hours after a soft-warning to let automated re-eval run without human interruption.

Immediate next steps (owners):

End of notes.
